qft-01-c1.text: University of Edinburgh, School of Physics and Astronomy (2006). Quantum Physics 2006/07, Lecture 15: Special Relativity Review; the Klein Gordon Equation. University of Edinburgh lecture notes.
qft-01-c1.quote: The candidate for the probability density, ρ(x), is no longer positive definite
qft-01-c1.claim: admits negative-energy solutions and a charge density that isn't positive-definite, so it can't serve as a probability density.

qft-07-c3.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (2004). The Nobel Prize in Physics 2004: Press release. NobelPrize.org.
qft-07-c3.quote: This discovery was expressed in 1973 in an elegant mathematical framework that led to a completely new theory
qft-07-c3.claim: This is asymptotic freedom, the 1973 result by Gross, Wilczek, and Politzer (Nobel 2004) that turned QCD from a candidate to the theory of strong interactions.

qft-09-c2.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (2013). The Nobel Prize in Physics 2013: Press release. NobelPrize.org.
qft-09-c2.quote: In 1964, they proposed the theory independently of each other (Englert together with his now deceased colleague Robert Brout).
qft-09-c2.claim: This is the Higgs mechanism (Anderson 1962; Brout, Englert, Higgs, Guralnik, Hagen, Kibble 1964).
